requirements.description: Add search filters allowing users to narrow results by category and city
requirements.label: needs_clarification

tasks.task: Gather requirements and confirm existing search capabilities (category and city fields available)
tasks.assumption: Assume platform has a searchable index with category and city attributes but no UI filters.

tasks.task: Design UI components for filter dropdowns (category, city) and integrate into search page
tasks.assumption: Assume existing front‑end framework allows adding new components without major redesign.

tasks.task: Implement backend query logic to apply category and city filters to search results
tasks.assumption: Assume the platform's search API can accept additional query parameters and supports filtering.

tasks.task: Update API endpoints / documentation to expose filter parameters and handle validation
tasks.assumption: Assume we have access to modify the API layer and can redeploy without breaking other features.

tasks.task: Testing: unit tests for backend, UI testing, QA verification across browsers
tasks.assumption: Assume test framework is in place and can be extended with new test cases.

requirements.description: Streamline the member addition process to reduce manual admin effort
requirements.label: needs_clarification

tasks.task: Analyze current member addition workflow and document manual steps
tasks.assumption: Admins currently add members one‑by‑one through a built‑in admin panel with no bulk or self‑service options.

tasks.task: Design and prototype a streamlined member addition UI (bulk upload CSV and optional self‑service registration form)
tasks.assumption: The platform allows custom front‑end components and can host uploaded files for processing.

tasks.task: Implement backend automation: create API endpoints, validation logic, CSV parsing, and email notifications
tasks.assumption: The platform provides an extensible backend (e.g., Node/Java/PHP) and access to the member database schema.

tasks.task: QA, integration testing, documentation, and admin training for the new workflow
tasks.assumption: A staging environment and test accounts are available for validation.

requirements.description: Implement a monthly newsletter that is sent only to members who have opted in
requirements.label: needs_clarification

tasks.task: Create and style the monthly newsletter email template and add a content management interface for editors
tasks.assumption: Platform includes a basic WYSIWYG editor or a content block system for managing email content.

tasks.task: Add/verify an opt‑in boolean field on the member profile and integrate the opt‑in UI into the registration and account settings pages
tasks.assumption: Member data model is extensible and the UI framework allows adding a simple checkbox.

tasks.task: Develop a backend service that assembles the newsletter (pulls dynamic content, applies the template) and queries only members with opt‑in = true
tasks.assumption: Platform provides a server‑side language/runtime (e.g., Node.js, PHP, Ruby) and a database query layer.

tasks.task: Configure a scheduled job (cron, task scheduler, or platform‑provided scheduler) to run the newsletter service once per month and send emails via the existing SMTP/mail service
tasks.assumption: An automated scheduler is available and the platform already has an email delivery service configured.

tasks.task: Test end‑to‑end flow: opt‑in handling, content rendering, email deliverability, unsubscribe link, and monthly trigger; fix any issues
tasks.assumption: Test environment mirrors production email sending capabilities.

requirements.description: Fix the mobile homepage layout so the menu does not overlap the logo and looks good on phones
requirements.label: needs_clarification

tasks.task: Investigate current mobile homepage layout to locate CSS/HTML causing the menu to overlap the logo and document required changes.
tasks.assumption: The site uses a responsive CSS framework (e.g., Bootstrap) and source files are accessible.

tasks.task: Update CSS (media queries or flex/grid rules) to reposition the menu so it no longer overlaps the logo on typical phone widths (320‑480 px).
tasks.assumption: The layout can be fixed with CSS adjustments without requiring a redesign of the header component.

tasks.task: If necessary, adjust the header markup (HTML) to improve the stacking order or element hierarchy for mobile view.
tasks.assumption: Minor markup changes are sufficient and will not impact other pages.

tasks.task: Perform functional and visual testing on multiple mobile devices and emulators (iOS, Android, various screen sizes) to confirm the fix works and does not introduce regressions.
tasks.assumption: Test devices/emulators are available and the QA process can be executed internally.

tasks.task: Deploy the CSS/HTML changes to the staging environment, obtain stakeholder sign‑off, then promote to production.
tasks.assumption: Standard CI/CD pipeline is in place and deployment windows are open.
